title: Detecting AI Impostors: How Do Middle Schoolers Identify LLM Agents in a Live Collaborative Setting?
abstract: arXiv:2608.30948v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLMs can imitate how people write, which raises concerns about impersonation, trust, and detection in social settings. These concerns are especially important for adolescents, who use generative AI frequently but may struggle to recognize it. We introduce \textit{DoppelBot}, a cooperative social deduction game designed to study how young people detect and respond to AI impersonation. Through studies with middle schoolers, we investigate whether a DoppelBot prompts reflection on privacy and impersonation, how repeated exposure affects AI-detection accuracy as agents become more personalized, and which strategies students use to identify AI doppelg\"angers. We find that students' detection accuracy improves over time, driven by a shift from relying on linguistic cues to leveraging shared social and contextual signals. translated_title: 检测AI冒充者：中学生如何在实时协作场景中识别大语言模型智能体？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型可以模仿人类的写作方式，这引发了关于社交场景中身份冒充、信任与检测的担忧。这些担忧对青少年尤为重要，因为他们频繁使用生成式AI，却可能难以识别它。我们提出了DoppelBot，一款旨在研究年轻人如何检测并应对AI冒充行为的合作式社交推理游戏。通过对中学生的研究，我们考察了DoppelBot是否能促使学生反思隐私与冒充问题、随着智能体日益个性化，反复接触如何影响AI检测的准确率，以及学生采用哪些策略来识别AI“分身”。我们发现，学生的检测准确率随时间推移而提升，其驱动力是从依赖语言线索转向利用共享的社交与情境信号。学生还表现出对AI局限性（如具身性缺失）的理解，并对更广泛的问题（如数据……）进行了反思。
tldr: 本文提出合作式社交推理游戏DoppelBot来研究中学生如何识别AI冒充者，发现学生的检测准确率随时间提升，其策略从依赖语言线索转向利用共享的社交与情境信号。
